stem:
A woman has lost 2.4 L of blood after birth. The team has repaired a cervical tear, treated atony and given tranexamic acid; the uterus is now firm, but diffuse oozing continues. Resuscitation, warming and red-cell replacement are underway. The anaesthetist reviews these urgent results:

| Investigation | Result | Local reference range |
|---|---:|---:|
| Fibrinogen | 1.1 g/L | 2.0–4.0 outside pregnancy |
| Platelets | 128 × 10⁹/L | 150–400 |
| INR | 1.2 | 0.9–1.2 |
| APTT | 31 s | 25–35 |

The listed products are immediately available. Which additional product most directly treats the demonstrated haemostatic deficit?

options.label: A
options.text: A further unit of packed red cells
options.explanation: Red cells support oxygen delivery during blood loss but do not provide the concentrated fibrinogen replacement needed for this result.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The fibrinogen is severely depleted during active bleeding. Cryoprecipitate provides targeted replacement even though INR and APTT remain near normal.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The platelet count is mildly reduced but well above the usual severe-bleeding replacement threshold; it does not explain the most marked measured deficit.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Prothrombin complex concentrate supplies selected clotting factors but does not adequately replace fibrinogen and is not the targeted product here.

options.label: E
options.text: Four units of fresh frozen plasma
options.explanation: Plasma contains fibrinogen but at a much lower concentration. With cryoprecipitate available and a dominant severe fibrinogen deficit, concentrated replacement is preferred.

context: In ongoing PPH, a very low fibrinogen needs targeted replacement; near-normal INR and APTT do not exclude a major haemostatic deficit.
